issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution repository introduces a different interface name 'Mountable' and has an effectively empty Rideable.java. Several concrete classes in the solution (Pig.java, Seal.java) implement Mountable instead of Rideable, while the template Main.java and the UML/spec refer to Rideable. This name/type mismatch between the expected interface and the solution implementation is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name and usage across all artifacts. Either (A) rename Mountable in the solution to Rideable and ensure Rideable.java declares String messageOnRide(); and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, or (B) update the problem statement/UML and template to reference Mountable consistently. Remove the unused/empty Rideable.java or make it the single interface required by the exercise so students see a consistent API to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a ride interface named 'Rideable', but the solution code introduces an interface named 'Mountable' (and leaves Rideable.java effectively empty). This is the same conceptual entity (an interface providing messageOnRide()), yet it is referenced with different identifiers across artifacts. Students following the problem/template will look for Rideable, while the solution and implemented classes (Pig, Seal) use Mountable, creating a confusing mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ride-interface identifier consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (or update the problem/template to use Mountable). Ensure the Rideable.java contains the interface declaration String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable. Remove or repurpose the empty Rideable.java to avoid duplicate/empty files.
